content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 11.1, ¶p0045).**

**What I found.** Section 11 contains three paragraphs pulling in opposite directions:

- **11.1** — walk-away language: immediate discontinuation of all assistance plus permanent deletion of Customer Data, expressly "without offering an export or migration support."
- **11.2** — compliant: 30-day return of all Customer Data in a documented, machine-readable format, with no fee-dispute hostage taking.
- **11.3** — compliant: secure deletion only *after* Customer confirms successful return, with officer certification and protection of any legally retained copy.

I also checked Section 10.1, which merely presumes "any agreed transition period" without obliging Vendor to grant one, so nothing elsewhere cures the gap. Section 16.5 routes Customer Data back to Sections 11 and 15, which makes the 11.1 conflict more consequential rather than less.

**Why it fails the fallback.** The rule's fallback needs 90 days of transition assistance plus a 30-day export. The Agreement offers zero days of assistance, and 11.1's immediate-deletion mandate would let Vendor destroy data before any 11.2 request could be made — the internal conflict is a live risk, not a drafting nit.

**The redline.** Smallest edit that reaches the preferred position: 11.1 is replaced with a six-month transition-assistance obligation at Vendor's then-current rates (including migration and export support), and any deletion is expressly subordinated to the existing 11.2/11.3 sequence. Sections 11.2 and 11.3 are left untouched since they already meet the preferred standard, and the comment offers 90 days as a fallback if Copperleaf pushes back on six months.
